Quiet, slightly overcast light settles over a dense central-Paris-style district. Roughly twenty tightly packed mid-rise perimeter blocks follow narrow streets and a few wider intersecting avenues. Irregular trapezoidal, triangular, and polygonal footprints bend to the angled roads; nearly continuous street-facing façades close around interior courtyards. Several courts remain visibly unfinished, with tall plain off-white inner walls and flat gray paving.

The blocks rise predominantly six to seven stories in a consistent Haussmannian rhythm: pale weathered stone, repetitive tall windows, black wrought-iron balcony rails, dark gray mansard roofs, dormer windows, chimneys, decorative cornices, and occasional arched blue or red doors. Close spacing makes urban canyons of the streets, while chamfered corners and wedge-shaped buildings give the junctions their form.

Below, dark asphalt roads meet broad gray stone sidewalks, painted lane arrows, dashed markings, zebra crossings, and small traffic islands. Black bollards and metal pedestrian railings line selected curbs. Traffic lights mark a prominent intersection, a red no-entry sign stands on a side street, and street signs and poles are scattered through the scene. Beside a corner bistro, a rack holds several bicycles; sparse young sidewalk trees, a few benches or café chairs, and occasional small street clutter accompany almost no people or vehicles.

The terrain stays flat. At the outer edges, abruptly cut building blocks, blank courtyard shells, and gray ground planes meet an empty pale sky, exposing the district’s unfinished margins.

Rebuild the place described above on the 200 m x 200 m plate, at the density
and arrangement the description calls for. Budget is 800 tool calls and 180

deterministic_rule_draft.prompt:
Quiet, slightly overcast light settles over a dense central-Paris-style district. Roughly twenty tightly packed mid-rise perimeter blocks follow narrow streets and a few wider intersecting avenues. Irregular trapezoidal, triangular, and polygonal footprints bend to the angled roads; nearly continuous street-facing façades close around interior courtyards. Several courts remain visibly unfinished, with tall plain off-white inner walls and flat gray paving.

The blocks rise predominantly six to seven stories in a consistent Haussmannian rhythm: pale weathered stone, repetitive tall windows, black wrought-iron balcony rails, dark gray mansard roofs, dormer windows, chimneys, decorative cornices, and occasional arched blue or red doors. Close spacing makes urban canyons of the streets, while chamfered corners and wedge-shaped buildings give the junctions their form.

Below, dark asphalt roads meet broad gray stone sidewalks, painted lane arrows, dashed markings, zebra crossings, and small traffic islands. Black bollards and metal pedestrian railings line selected curbs. Traffic lights mark a prominent intersection, a red no-entry sign stands on a side street, and street signs and poles are scattered through the scene. Beside a corner bistro, a rack holds several bicycles; sparse young sidewalk trees, a few benches or café chairs, and occasional small street clutter accompany almost no people or vehicles.

The terrain stays flat. At the outer edges, abruptly cut building blocks, blank courtyard shells, and gray ground planes meet an empty pale sky, exposing the district’s unfinished margins.
